title: Homotopically surjective simplicial-presheaf model map
statement: Use the universe conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]; the model-category conventions used below are stated explicitly in this node. Categories are complete and cocomplete, weak equivalences satisfy two-out-of-three and retract closure, and (cofibrations, trivial fibrations) and (trivial cofibrations, fibrations) are weak factorization systems with functorial factorizations. A weak factorization system consists of mutually characterized left and right diagonal-lifting classes and factorizations of all arrows; trivial means also a weak equivalence. Cofibrant and fibrant mean that the initial and terminal maps, respectively, are cofibrations and fibrations. A cofibrant replacement is a trivial fibration $QX\to X$ with $QX$ cofibrant; a fibrant replacement is a trivial cofibration $X\to TX$ with $TX$ fibrant. Combinatorial means locally presentable with small generating sets $I,J$ whose right lifting classes are the trivial fibrations and fibrations, respectively. Locally presentable means cocomplete and generated, for some regular $\kappa$, under $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects whose ordinary Hom functors preserve these colimits. A Quillen adjunction is an ordinary adjunction whose left adjoint preserves cofibrations and trivial cofibrations. It is a Quillen equivalence when, for each cofibrant source object $A$ and fibrant target object $Y$, a map $LA\to Y$ is a weak equivalence if and only if its adjoint $A\to RY$ is a weak equivalence. Write $\mathsf{sSet}$ for the simplicial sets of [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] with the Kan model structure: cofibrations are monomorphisms; fibrations have the right lifting property against all horns $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ ($n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$), where $\Delta^n$ is the representable simplex and $\Lambda_i^n$ is the union of its faces other than the $i$th; weak equivalences induce a bijection on path components and isomorphisms on all homotopy groups of geometric realizations. Let $\mathcal M$ be combinatorial. There exist a small ordinary category $D$ and a Quillen adjunction $L_0:\mathsf U(D)\rightleftarrows\mathcal M:R_0$, where $\mathsf U(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{sSet})$ has the projective model structure (objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations, and cofibrations defined by the left lifting property against trivial fibrations), such that for every fibrant $X$ in $\mathcal M$ and every cofibrant replacement $q:QR_0X\to R_0X$, the counit composite $L_0QR_0X\xrightarrow{L_0q}L_0R_0X\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_X}X$ is a weak equivalence. A Quillen adjunction with this counit property is called homotopically surjective.

proof.text: Choose $\lambda,B,C,E,R,\eta,Q$ from the bounded-resolution theorem. Its conclusions supply all three hypotheses of the cofibrant-density theorem: local $\lambda$-presentability, preservation of weak equivalences by $\lambda$-filtered colimits, and a cofibrant replacement preserving $\lambda$-presentable objects. Let $D\subset E$ consist of the cosimplicial resolutions and let $\gamma:D\to\mathcal M$ be evaluation at zero. The category $D$ is small by the cited theorem (equivalently, after choosing $B$, a cosimplicial object is countably many choices of objects and arrows from small sets). Its inclusion $A:D\to\mathcal M^\Delta$ supplies cosimplicial resolutions with $A_d^0=\gamma(d)$. Small representative choices throughout are fixed as in that theorem; equalities using these choices mean the specified natural identifications.

source.place: Section 6.2 and the construction of R in Lemma 6.3, printed pp. 189-190.

proof.text: Give $\mathsf U(D)$ the projective model structure from the cited existing node; this has the required objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations. Apply the cosimplicial-presheaf counit theorem to the resolution-valued functor $A$. It constructs an ordinary adjunction $L_A\dashv R_A$, with $(R_AX)(d)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(A_d^n,X)$ and left adjoint the indicated coend, and proves that it is Quillen. Set $L_0=L_A$ and $R_0=R_A$. No simplicial structure on $\mathcal M$ is used.

source.place: Sections 4 and 6.2, printed pp. 183-184, 189; Universal Homotopy Theories, Proposition 3.4 and Section 9.5, pp. 155, 171-172.

proof.text: Fix any $X\in\mathcal M$. Put $I=(C\downarrow X)$ and $J=(\gamma\downarrow X)$, with value diagrams $V(c,u)=c$ and $Vf(A,u)=A^0$, respectively. Evaluation gives $f:J\to I$. Define $r:I\to J$ by $r(c,u)=(R\operatorname{const}c,u)$; its degree-zero map is $u$ since $R$ fixes degree zero. Thus $fr=\mathrm{id}_I$. Define $H:J\to J$ by $H(A,u)=(RA,u)$. These are functors into $D$ by the bounded-resolution theorem. The transformations $\eta_A:RA\to A$ and $R(A\to\operatorname{const}A^0):RA\to R\operatorname{const}A^0$ give $H\to\mathrm{id}_J$ and $H\to rf$, over $X$. The second map uses the canonical cosimplicial augmentation; at degree zero both transformations are identities. Hence every component becomes an identity under the degree-zero value diagram. The reindexing-zigzag theorem, with $g=f$ and inverse functor $r$, therefore proves that $f_*:\operatorname{hocolim}_J A^0\to\operatorname{hocolim}_I c$ is an isomorphism in the homotopy category. The construction uses the value diagram, not just an equivalence between indexing nerves.

source.place: Lemma 6.3 and Proposition A.4 / Remark A.5, printed pp. 189-190, 198-199.

proof.text: The cofibrant-density theorem applies to $C$ with the cardinal and replacement from Step 1. It gives the weak-equivalence augmentation $a:\operatorname{hocolim}_{(C\downarrow X)}c\to X$. The comparison $f_*$ of Step 3 respects augmentations: its cocone component at $(A,u)$ is the same map $u:A^0\to X$ as the component after evaluation at zero. Thus the naive resolution augmentation $b:\operatorname{hocolim}_{(\gamma\downarrow X)}A^0\to X$ equals $af_*$ in the homotopy category. The density and reindexing theorems consequently make $b$ a weak equivalence.

source.place: Proposition 4.7(ii) and the left-hand triangle in the general proof of Proposition 3.3, printed pp. 187, 191.

proof.text: For every $n\geq0$ form $I_n=(A^n\downarrow X)$ with value $A^0$, as in the degree-reduction theorem. The collapse $p:[n]\to[0]$ gives $i_n:I_0\to I_n$, $(A,u)\mapsto(A,uA(p))$. The last vertex $v:[0]\to[n]$ gives $j_n:I_n\to I_0$, $(A,u)\mapsto(A,uA(v))$. Since $pv=1$, $j_ni_n=\mathrm{id}_{I_0}$. The monotone function $[n]\times[1]\to[n]$ given by $(k,0)\mapsto k$ and $(k,1)\mapsto n$ induces a simplicial map $h:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^n$ from the identity to $vp$. Its monotonicity follows because every $k\leq n$, including when the second coordinate increases. Compose $h$ with the symmetry $\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\cong\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$. The identification $A\otimes_\Delta\Delta^n\cong A^n$ sends the summand $A^r$ indexed by $\alpha:[r]\to[n]$ by $A(\alpha)$; its inverse is the coprojection indexed by $1_{[n]}$, and the coend relations show that the two composites are identities. Applying the interval-tensor coend with this identification gives a natural map $t_A:(A\otimes\Delta^1)^n\to A^n$ whose endpoint composites are $1_{A^n}$ and $A(vp)$. Define $H_n:I_n\to I_n$ by $(A,u)\mapsto(A\otimes\Delta^1,ut_A)$. The interval-tensor theorem ensures that $A\otimes\Delta^1$ is still a resolution with $\lambda$-presentable terms, hence is an object of $D$ after the fixed representative transport. Its endpoint maps give natural transformations $\mathrm{id}_{I_n}\to H_n$ and $i_nj_n\to H_n$: the required equalities over $X$ are respectively $ut_Ae_0=u$ and $ut_Ae_1=uA(vp)$. On the value diagram $A^0$, both transformations are weak equivalences by the objectwise endpoint clause of the interval theorem. The other composite $j_ni_n$ is the identity, so the reindexing-zigzag theorem applies to $g=i_n$, inverse functor $j_n$. It proves that $(i_n)_*:\operatorname{hocolim}_{I_0}A^0\to\operatorname{hocolim}_{I_n}A^0$ is an isomorphism for every $n$. For $n=0$, both functors are identities and the same formulas apply.

source.place: Lemma 6.4 and Appendix A.1, printed pp. 190-191, 197; explicit last-vertex contraction supplies the detail left to the reader.

proof.text: Apply the degree-reduction theorem to $A:D\to\mathcal M^\Delta$. Its hypothesis for every $n$ is exactly Step 5; $D$ is small and its values are Reedy cofibrant and homotopically constant by Step 1. We obtain an isomorphism $i_*:\operatorname{hocolim}_{I_0}A^0\to\operatorname{hocolim}_{K_X}T_X$ in the homotopy category, where $K_X$ records all pairs $(A,[n])$ mapping by $A^n\to X$ and $T_X$ takes the value $A^n$. The theorem includes augmentation compatibility, so if $c_X:\operatorname{hocolim}_{K_X}T_X\to X$ is the canonical augmentation, $c_Xi_*=b$. The actual homotopy-colimit comparison representing $i_*$ is a weak equivalence by the degree-reduction theorem. Since $b$ is a weak equivalence by Step 4 and $c_Xi_*=b$, two-out-of-three shows that $c_X$ is a weak equivalence. In this argument the degree-$n$ diagram has value $A^0$ and the total diagram has value $A^n$; they are not identified.

source.place: Proposition 4.6 and the general proof of Proposition 3.3, printed pp. 186, 191.

proof.text: Now assume $X$ fibrant and let $q:QR_0X\to R_0X$ be any projective cofibrant replacement. The cosimplicial-presheaf counit theorem applies to this specific $q$ and identifies the arrow $\varepsilon_XL_0q$ with $c_X$ in the slice $\operatorname{Ho}(\mathcal M)/X$. Its final clause says exactly that the former is a weak equivalence when the latter is. Step 6 gives that condition. Thus the required counit composite is a weak equivalence for every fibrant $X$ and every such $q$, which is the definition of homotopical surjectivity in the item. Together with the smallness of $D$ and the Quillen adjunction in Step 2 this proves the whole statement.

source.place: Definition 3.1, Proposition 4.2, Corollary 4.4 and conclusion of Section 6, printed pp. 181, 184-185, 191.
